BoyerMooreSearch.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes a string-search instance by storing the input text and pattern as instance attributes alongside their precomputed lengths for efficient reuse in search operations." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> text </REF>: str "The source string to be searched"
        <REF> pattern </REF>: str "The pattern string to search for within text"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign the caller-supplied text argument to self.text and the caller-supplied pattern argument to self.pattern in a single simultaneous assignment, storing direct references with no transformation RESULT self.text, self.pattern]
            [COMMAND Compute len(text) and len(pattern) from the original caller-supplied arguments and assign the resulting non-negative integers to self.textLen and self.patLen respectively in a single simultaneous assignment RESULT self.textLen, self.patLen]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: Either text or pattern does not implement __len__]
        [LOG "len() raises TypeError when called on an object that has no __len__ method"]
        [THROW TypeError "Raised by the built-in len() call on line 2 if text or pattern is not a length-supporting object"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
BoyerMooreSearch.match_in_pattern:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Searches the pattern string from right to left for the rightmost occurrence of a given character and returns its index, or -1 if not found." match_in_pattern]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> char </REF>: character "The character to search for within the pattern string"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: integer "The index of the rightmost occurrence of char in the pattern, or -1 if char is not present"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Iterate i from patLen - 1 down to 0 inclusive, stepping by -1, covering all valid indices of the pattern from right to left RESULT loop_index_i]
            [COMMAND Within the reverse loop over i, compare char against the character at position i in the pattern using an equality check RESULT match_found]
            [COMMAND Within the reverse loop, if the equality check is true, immediately return i as the result, exiting both the loop and the method RESULT early_return_index]
            [COMMAND After the loop completes without finding a match, return -1 to indicate that char does not appear anywhere in the pattern RESULT default_return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: char is found at the last index of the pattern (i = patLen - 1) on the first iteration]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return patLen - 1 immediately on the first iteration without advancing the loop further RESULT early_return_index]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: patLen is 0, causing range(self.patLen - 1, -1, -1) to produce an empty sequence]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the loop body entirely and proceed directly to return -1 RESULT default_return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
BoyerMooreSearch.mismatch_in_text:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Scans the pattern against the text substring starting at currentPos in right-to-left order and returns the absolute text index of the rightmost mismatched character, or -1 if all characters match." mismatch_in_text]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> currentPos </REF>: int "The starting position in the text at which the pattern alignment begins; used as a base offset when computing text character indices."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: int "The absolute index in the text of the rightmost mismatched character (currentPos + i) if a mismatch is found, or -1 if every character in the pattern matches the corresponding text character."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Iterate i from (self.patLen - 1) down to 0 inclusive, stepping by -1, traversing the pattern from its last character to its first in right-to-left order. RESULT loop_index_i]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over i, compare self.pattern[i] against self.text[currentPos + i]; if they are not equal, immediately return the value (currentPos + i), which is the absolute index in the text where the mismatch was found, and exit the method. RESULT early_return_mismatch_index]
            [COMMAND After the for loop completes without triggering any early return, return -1 to signal that all pattern characters matched the corresponding text characters at the given alignment. RESULT return_full_match_sentinel]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: self.patLen is 0, making range(self.patLen - 1, -1, -1) an empty range.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the for loop body entirely because the range produces no iterations, then fall through to return -1. RESULT return_full_match_sentinel]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
BoyerMooreSearch.bad_character_heuristic:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Searches for all occurrences of the pattern in the text using the Boyer-Moore bad-character heuristic, returning a list of starting positions where the pattern fully matches." bad_character_heuristic]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance providing textLen (length of text), patLen (length of pattern), text (the string being searched), mismatch_in_text(i) which returns the text index of the first mismatch when aligning the pattern at position i or -1 on a full match, and match_in_pattern(char) which returns the rightmost index of char in the pattern or a value causing a safe shift when absent"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> positions </REF>: list "List of integer starting indices in the text at which the pattern was found to fully match"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize positions as an empty list RESULT positions]
            [COMMAND Iterate i over the integer range from 0 up to and including textLen - patLen (i.e., range(textLen - patLen + 1)), covering every valid alignment position where the pattern fits without overrunning the text RESULT loop_i]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, call mismatch_in_text(i) to obtain the text index of the first character that does not match the pattern when aligned at position i, or -1 if the entire pattern matches; store the result RESULT mismatch_index]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, if mismatch_index equals -1 (full match), append i to positions RESULT positions]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, if mismatch_index is not -1 (mismatch occurred), call match_in_pattern with the character text[mismatch_index] to obtain the rightmost occurrence index of that character in the pattern, then assign i = mismatch_index - match_index as the intended bad-character shift; NOTE: this assignment has no effect in a Python for-loop because the loop variable is rebound from the iterator at the start of each iteration, so the skip is never applied and the loop always advances by 1 RESULT match_index]
            [COMMAND After the loop completes, return positions RESULT positions]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: patLen equals textLen: only one alignment position exists (i = 0), so the loop executes exactly once]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call mismatch_in_text(0); if it returns -1, positions contains [0]; otherwise positions remains empty RESULT positions]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: patLen is greater than textLen: range(textLen - patLen + 1) is empty, so the loop body never executes]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return positions as an empty list immediately RESULT positions]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
